model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Republican lean, Gill's roughly 200-to-1 fundraising edge, and market pricing near 98 percent Republican all point the same direction, and no polling or expert ratings suggest the race is in play. A modest nudge beyond the fundamentals-based estimate reflects the challenger's near-total lack of resources.
model.watch: A strongly favorable national environment for Democrats or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signals that could move this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Texas's 26th District, anchored in the northern Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs, leans about eleven points Republican, and first-term Representative Brandon Gill is seeking a second term. Gill has built one of the larger war chests among House freshmen, reporting roughly $7.9 million raised and more than $2 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Steven Shook, has raised about $36,000, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public general-election polling tracks the race, and no national ratings list it as competitive. Prediction markets put Republican odds near 98 percent. The forecast therefore rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the absence of any visible challenger infrastructure. A sharply favorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the expected margin, but the seat remains firmly in the Republican column.
